title: Relations (III') and (IV) of Nakamura and Schneps hold on the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, with an application to the two elliptic points of the modular curve
subject: math.GR
abstract: Nakamura and Schneps (2000) defined a subgroup $\mathrm{I}\Gamma$ of the profinite Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ by two relations, $(\mathrm{III}')$ and $(\mathrm{IV})$, that hold for Galois elements; they proved that it acts on the profinite mapping class groups of all surfaces, and left open whether it is all of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. We prove that $(\mathrm{IV})$ holds for every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. It follows that every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is the product of a Galois element and an element of the group $\Lambda$ of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, which acts on the whole tower of pure mapping class groups by their formulas. As an application we study a character $\delta$ with values in $\mathbf F_2$, defined on the larger group given by the two- and three-cycle relations alone, which compares at level twelve how an element moves the two elliptic points of the modular curve. We prove that $\delta$ vanishes on the normalized elements of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, so that every character extending it and trivial on Galois elements is trivial on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Version 2 adds three things. First, $(\mathrm{III}')$ also holds for every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$; so $\mathrm{I}\Gamma=\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, and the representations of $\mathrm{I}\Gamma$ in the automorphism groups of all profinite mapping class groups, constructed by Nakamura and Schneps, are representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Second, the questions that Lochak (2025) asks about his groups of compatible pairs have a positive answer: these groups are $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, and by his theorem $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is then the group of inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of the procongruence mapping class group of every surface of generic type and positive genus. Third, a correction: version 1 called the strictness of the inclusion of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ in the larger group known, and we have found no published proof of it. The proofs use the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite $p$-subgroups of profinite completions, the action of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, and the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. The mathematics of version 1 was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode); it was checked by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, which wrote this text and rewrote several proofs, and by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max as second reader. The additions of version 2 are by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, one of them with Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max; the new theorem and its two corollaries were checked by a second reader, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, in a separate run. No human has checked any of it.
comments:
Version 2 (24 November 2026): version 1 is unchanged. New: relation (III') holds for every element of GT-hat (Theorem 20), so the subgroup I-Gamma of Nakamura and Schneps is all of GT-hat (Corollary 21); Lochak's questions on compatible pairs (Algebra i Analiz 37:2, 2025) are answered, and with his Theorem 5.10 the inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of the procongruence mapping class group of every surface of generic type form GT-hat (Corollary 22). Corrected: version 1 called the strictness of GT-hat in the gentle group known; no published proof was found.

Relation (IV) is H. Nakamura's; the subgroup it defines with (III') is Nakamura and Schneps's (Invent. Math. 2000), who proved that Galois elements satisfy it and left open whether the subgroup is all of GT-hat; Lochak, Nakamura and Schneps (February 2026) still called this unclear. The group Lambda and its action on the tower are Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps's; the implication from the normalized relation (IV) to their relation (R) is Schneps's. The proofs rest on the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite p-subgroups of profinite mapping class groups and on the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. New here: (IV) on all of GT-hat, the decomposition GT-hat = Lambda_0 . G_Q, and the vanishing of the level-twelve character delta on normalized elements (version 1); (III') on all of GT-hat, hence I-Gamma = GT-hat, and the positive answer to the questions of Lochak on compatible pairs (version 2).

Checks: Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked the proofs of version 1 and wrote the text; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max refereed version 1 as second reader. Theorem 20 and Corollaries 21-22 (by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max) were checked by a second reader, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, and read again before deposit. No human has checked it. provenance:
Text: AI-authored; none of it was written by a human. The submitter takes responsibility for the veracity of the text.

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, produced the mathematics in research runs of November 2026 on notes of Grothendieck's La longue marche a travers la theorie de Galois, prompted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max. Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote the present text on 23 November 2026 as editor, rewriting several proofs (the finite-subgroup steps through Boggi-Zalesskii, the shear lemma, the unit lemma, half of one proposition). On 24 November 2026 Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, made version 2: it found and proved Theorem 20 (relation (III')) and Corollary 21, re-derived Corollary 22, which Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort max, had proved in substance in a survey of connections, and added Remarks 19 and 23. An earlier run of GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) of 16 November 2026 had proved Theorem 1 in Lochak's formulation.

How it was checked. Claude Fable 5.2, at effort max, checked every step of the runs' proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 (18 November), re-proved the final computation independently (21 November) and checked the chain behind the hexagonal self-similarity (23 November). Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, checked the parity computation exhaustively over Z/12 with its own program (22 November) and, as second reader (23 November), followed every step of Sections 4 and 8 and of the rewritten proofs, re-derived the matrix and braid identities, opened Hoshi-Minamide-Mochizuki at the source and found no mathematical error. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read the text again before deposit and recomputed the steps behind Theorems 1 and 2. A remark on a character Delta of the larger group is cited from the runs and marked as not refereed; it is not used in the theorems. arXiv, the web and Hexagon were searched on 23 November 2026. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized. Theorem 20 and Corollaries 21-22 were checked by a second reader, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, in a separate run (24 November 2026): every step was followed and the braid and abelianization identities recomputed; Nakamura-Schneps 2000 (Theorem 1.1, Definition 1.1, Theorems 1.3-1.4), Boggi-Zalesskii Theorem A(iii), Furusho 2002 (p. 191) and Lochak 2025 (Definitions 5.4 and 5.8, Proposition-Definition 5.6, Theorem 5.10, pp. 61-62) were opened at the statements used. The statement of Lochak's Theorem 5.10 ii) and the labels of his relations were then read on the printed page by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max read the proof of Theorem 20 step by step and the changed pages again before deposit. Remark 19 has been checked by its author only. Lochak's Theorem 5.10 and Nakamura and Schneps's Theorems 1.3 and 1.4 are used as published, and their proofs were not checked. The statement of version 1 that the strictness of the inclusion of GT-hat in the gentle group is known was wrong as a statement about the literature and is corrected.
